text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I ran perf + flamegraph on prod-dedicated-3 against the long-tail inference workload. CPU hotspot is on the CPU side: Python scheduler + tokenization boundary, and a bunch of time spent in KV-cache eviction callbacks that run under the scheduler lock. Attaching notes below.

Maria: Can you paste the perf command and a short flamegraph snippet?

Alex: Ran:```perf record -F 99 -a -g -- python3 run_inference_benchmark.py --seq 1024 --concurrency 8```Flamegraph top stacks (summary):
- PyEval_EvalFrameEx -> scheduler.schedule_batch -> tokenize_batch -> acquire_lock -> handle_kv_miss -> memcpy
- scheduler.poll -> wait_on_condition -> PyEval_EvalFrameEx

Raj: Are worker threads pinned / CPU affinity correct? Also ensure frame pointers / call graph options are valid for CPython. For accurate Python stacks I'd usually run with:```perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -p <pid>```or use py-spy / perf-tools.

Alex: Re-ran with --call-graph dwarf and a second run using py-spy. py-spy shows a lot of time in PyUnicode_Decode and in the Python-level tokenizer converting bytes->str per token.

Jen: Could that be because we decode every token at the Python boundary instead of working with raw bytes in C/C++? If so we should push tokenization into a C extension or a Rust tokenizer.

Maria: Also the KV cache path looks suspicious. The flamegraph shows handle_kv_miss holding the scheduler lock and then calling back into Python: eviction callback -> py side. Evictions spike when per-shard cache fullness hits ~95%.

Alex: Logs excerpt:```[2026-03-17T14:02:11.234Z] shard-3 evict key=0x7fcb... reason=capacity
[2026-03-17T14:02:11.235Z] handle_kv_miss: entering eviction callback -> py_callback_handle_eviction
[2026-03-17T14:02:11.238Z] eviction done (t=3ms)```Stack samples show GIL held during the callback.

Raj: Quick experiments to try: 1) bump per-shard cache cap 2x and re-run to see if evictions are the root cause; 2) move eviction handling off the scheduler thread; 3) use gil_scoped_release for the python callback path if we can't avoid calling Python. Also confirm thread affinity and repeat perf with frame pointers enabled.

Alex: Bumped cache cap to 2x and re-ran. Tail latencies improved (p99 down ~12%) but overall Python CPU time is still high. That suggests two issues:KV evictions amplify stalls, but tokenization/GIL work is a separate contributor.

Jen: I'll prototype a C tokenizer POC (Rust tokenizer binding) to eliminate Python-level decode overhead. If tokenization moves into C there should be a measurable drop in PyEval time.

Maria: On batching heuristics — current aggregator waits up to 12ms to coalesce requests. For low-QPS workloads that causes more frequent scheduling wakes and more Python scheduler activity. Try increasing the wait to 20ms for low-QPS configs and measure.

Alex: Additional profiling notes: py-spy samples show repeated frames: PyUnicode_Decode, tokenize_batch (py), bytes->str conversion. perf dwarf run shows consistent call-chains into memcpy and decode functions. Suggest we: 1) add gil_scoped_release around eviction callback work, 2) refactor eviction callbacks into a background C++ thread queue, 3) move tokenization into native code, 4) experiment with batching timeout for low-QPS.

Raj: One more perf flag: when building perf-friendly builds, compile CPython C extensions with -fno-omit-frame-pointer and enable -g to make DWARF stacks more reliable. Also check kernel perf_event_paranoid on the host.

Alex: Action items and ownership:
- Alex: implement and bench gil_scoped_release in eviction path + open PR with before/after flamegraphs.
- Jen: tokenizer POC (Rust/C) + microbench.
- Raj: validate CPU affinity, repeat perf runs with --call-graph dwarf and advise on perf-friendly build flags.
- Maria: run the config sweep for batching timeout and repeat benchmark for cache caps.

perf-bot: Benchmark run complete: p99 latency -14%, overall CPU user time -9% (after local PR patch branch that defers eviction callbacks).

Jen: I'll start the tokenizer POC today, aim to have a microbench by EOD.

Alex: I'll open the PR for the eviction change and attach perf + flamegraph artifacts. Thanks all.

ci-bot: CI: benchmark job queued #4567 (will run after PR).

Alex: We'll reconvene after the PR and tokenizer microbench results. If anyone sees a regression or wants to rerun specific traces, ping me in-thread or drop flamegraphs in the artifacts channel.
